The core insight of Silent Impact lies in leveraging passive-arm IMU data for shot classification without relying on dominant-arm impact jerks. The method employs a 1D CNN with frequency-band decomposition and attention mechanisms. The frequency bands (0–4 Hz, 5–20 Hz, >20 Hz) isolate whole-body motion, upper-body swing, and impact vibration respectively. These are processed through a modified CNN with attention blocks that weight relevant temporal features. The shot detection model uses MS-TCN for binary classification, refined via post-processing. The classification model achieves 88.2% accuracy on passive-arm data, close to 90.1% on dominant-arm data. This suggests that passive-arm sensing can be viable for wearable applications, though the label generation still relies on dominant-arm data, introducing a critical dependency. The model's robustness is limited by small sample size and lack of generalizability across skill levels and body types. The derived operators—frequency-band attention and temporal attention blocks—are mathematically grounded in signal processing and deep learning principles, enabling modular reuse in GSE's wearable analytics framework.
